description: A commercial invoice used in international and domestic trade to document the sale of goods between a seller and buyer, including shipment details, item descriptions, and totals, serving as the primary document for customs, payment, and accounting purposes.
A seller's residential property disclosure statement capturing known material defects, conditions, and features of a property being sold, as reported by the seller.
ACORD 125 Commercial Insurance Application — captures applicant, business, coverage, and general underwriting information for commercial lines submissions.

ACORD 126 (2016/03) Commercial General Liability Section — supplemental CGL application capturing coverage details, limits, premises, operations, products, subcontractors, and loss history. Typically attached to ACORD 125.

ACORD 127 Business Auto Section — supplemental automobile schedule attached to a commercial lines submission (typically ACORD 125), capturing vehicle, driver, and coverage details for business auto policies.

ACORD 130 Workers Compensation Application — captures agency/producer, applicant, policy, operations, classification, experience, loss history, underwriting, and coverage information for a workers compensation insurance submission.

ACORD 140 Property Section — supplemental property insurance application capturing location, building construction, occupancy, protection, and coverage details for commercial lines submissions, typically attached to an ACORD 125 Commercial Lines Application.
ACORD 22 Evidence of Property Insurance form — provides evidence of property insurance coverage to a certificate holder, mortgagee, or other interested party for a described property location.
ACORD 24 Certificate of Property Insurance — documents property coverage in force for a named insured and lists coverage details, locations, and certificate holders.
ACORD 27 Evidence of Property Insurance form — provides certificate-level evidence of commercial property coverage to a designated certificate holder, mortgagee, or other interested party.
ACORD 28 Evidence of Commercial Property Insurance — documents coverage details for a specific property location for the benefit of a certificate holder, lender, or additional interest party.
ACORD 35 — Cancellation/Expiration Notice, used by insurers and agents to notify insureds of policy cancellation or expiration.
ACORD 36 — Cancellation Request/Policy Release form used to request cancellation of an in-force insurance policy and authorize release of the policy by the insurer.
ACORD 50 — Automobile Loss Notice capturing first-notice-of-loss information for personal and commercial auto claims.
ACORD 75 — Surplus Lines Disclosure form used to notify insureds that coverage is being placed with a non-admitted surplus lines insurer, and to document the associated premium tax information.
ACORD 90 — Umbrella/Excess Liability Application, used to apply for umbrella or excess liability insurance coverage for commercial risks.

ADA Dental Claim Form (J400 series, 2006/2012/2019 revisions) used to submit dental procedure claims to insurers and government payers, capturing payer, policyholder, patient, provider, and procedure information.

Application for Certificate of Citizenship (Form N-600), filed with USCIS by a U.S. citizen parent on behalf of a minor child, or by an adult claiming citizenship acquired or derived through a U.S. citizen parent.

CBP Form 3461 (Entry/Immediate Delivery) — U.S. Customs and Border Protection form used to request release of imported merchandise from CBP custody before duties are paid and before filing a formal entry summary (CBP Form 7501).

CFPB Closing Disclosure (Form H-25) — the standardized five-page mortgage settlement statement provided to borrowers at least three business days before closing, detailing final loan terms, projected payments, closing costs, and cash to close.

CFPB-mandated Loan Estimate form (TRID/TILA-RESPA Integrated Disclosure, form H-24), provided to mortgage applicants within three business days of application. Discloses key loan terms, projected payments, and estimated closing costs across three standardized pages.
CMS-10106 Authorization to Disclose Personal Health Information — authorizes Medicare to release a beneficiary's personal health information to a designated person or organization.
CMS-1490S Patient's Request for Medical Payment form, used by Medicare beneficiaries to submit out-of-pocket medical claims directly to Medicare for reimbursement.

CMS-1763 Request for Earnings and Benefit Estimate Statement — a single-record form submitted to the Social Security Administration by an individual requesting a copy of their Social Security earnings record and a benefit estimate.

CMS-40B — Application for Enrollment in Medicare Part B (Medical Insurance), used by individuals who are eligible for Medicare and wish to enroll in or be reinstated for Part B (Supplementary Medical Insurance) coverage.

CMS-460 Medicare Participating Physician or Supplier Agreement, the form by which a physician, supplier, or group practice enrolls as a Medicare participating provider and agrees to accept assignment on all Medicare claims.

CMS-485 Home Health Certification and Plan of Care form used to certify Medicare home health eligibility and document the patient's plan of care, including diagnoses, orders, functional limitations, medications, and physician certification.

CMS-588 Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) Authorization Agreement used by Medicare providers and suppliers to enroll in, change, or cancel direct deposit of Medicare payments to a financial institution.

CMS-855 Medicare Enrollment Application — captures provider/supplier identity, practice location, ownership, managing employee, billing agency, adverse legal actions, and certification data submitted to Medicare for enrollment, revalidation, or change of information.

CMS-855A Medicare Enrollment Application for Institutional Providers, used by hospitals, skilled nursing facilities, home health agencies, hospices, and other institutional providers to enroll in, revalidate, or update their Medicare participation.

CMS-855B Medicare Enrollment Application for Clinics/Group Practices and Certain Other Suppliers — used by organizations (non-individuals) to enroll in Medicare or to report changes to an existing enrollment.

CMS-855I Medicare Enrollment Application for Individual Physicians and Non-Physician Practitioners — captures all sections of the form used to enroll an individual practitioner in Medicare or to make changes to an existing enrollment.
CMS-L564 Request for Employment Information form, used by Medicare applicants to document employer-sponsored group health plan coverage for Special Enrollment Period purposes.

CMS-R-131 Advance Beneficiary Notice of Noncoverage (ABN) — the standardized Medicare notice given to a beneficiary before receiving items or services that Medicare may deny as not reasonable and necessary, capturing notifier information, items/services with reasons and estimated costs, and the beneficiary's option election and signature.
DD Form 1351-2 — Travel Voucher or Subvoucher, the standard DoD travel reimbursement claim form for military and civilian travelers.
DD Form 2058 (State of Legal Residence Certificate) — used by military members to declare or change their state of legal residence for state income tax withholding purposes.
DD Form 256, Honorable Discharge Certificate issued to U.S. military service members upon honorable separation from active duty or reserve service.

DD Form 2656 (Data for Payment of Retired Personnel) — the retirement application form used by U.S. military members to provide personal and dependency data, elect Survivor Benefit Plan coverage, designate beneficiaries, and set up direct deposit and tax withholding for DFAS retired pay.

DD Form 2808, Report of Medical Examination — the U.S. military physical examination form completed by an examining physician documenting a service member's or applicant's administrative information, vital measurements, medical history, system-by-system examination findings, laboratory results, and overall fitness determination.
Declaration for Federal Employment (OF-306), used by applicants for U.S. federal civilian positions to disclose background information required for employment suitability and security determinations.

DoD Form DD-2807 (Report of Medical History) — the self-reported medical history questionnaire completed by an applicant, recruit, or servicemember prior to a military physical examination. Used during entrance, separation, periodic, and other military medical examinations to document self-reported health history and current status.
Explanation of Benefits (EOB) issued by a health insurance payer summarizing how a claim was adjudicated — what was billed, what the plan paid, and what the member owes.
FEC Form 3 — Report of Receipts and Disbursements for an Authorized Committee of a House or Senate candidate committee.

FEC Form 3X — Report of Receipts and Disbursements for an Authorized Committee (PAC, party committee, or other non-candidate committee), covering cover-page identification, summary financial totals, and itemized schedules.

Federal Civil Cover Sheet JS-44 (Rev. 04/21), filed with a civil complaint in U.S. District Courts to provide the clerk with statistical information and initiate or supplement pleadings as required by local rules.
FinCEN Form 111 Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) — the Bank Secrecy Act filing used by financial institutions to report known or suspected violations of law or suspicious transactions to FinCEN.
FinCEN Form 112 Currency Transaction Report (CTR), used by financial institutions to report cash transactions exceeding $10,000 to the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network.

FinCEN Form 114 (Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts, FBAR) — annual disclosure filed electronically via BSA E-Filing by U.S. persons who have a financial interest in or signature authority over foreign financial accounts with an aggregate value exceeding $10,000 at any point during the calendar year.

Form 1040, U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, is the primary IRS form used by U.S. individual taxpayers to report annual income, calculate tax liability, and claim credits and deductions for the tax year January 1–December 31, 2025.

Form 1041 (U.S. Income Tax Return for Estates and Trusts) is filed by the fiduciary of a domestic decedent's estate, trust, or bankruptcy estate to report income, deductions, gains, losses, and tax liability for the entity.

Form 1065, U.S. Return of Partnership Income, is filed by domestic partnerships with the IRS to report the partnership's income, deductions, gains, losses, and other financial information for the tax year.

Form 1098 (Mortgage Interest Statement) is filed by a recipient/lender to report mortgage interest of $600 or more received from a payer/borrower during the calendar year to the Internal Revenue Service.

Form 1098-T (Tuition Statement) is filed by eligible educational institutions to report payments received for qualified tuition and related expenses, scholarships or grants, and other education-related amounts for each enrolled student to the IRS and the student.

Form 1099-DIV (Rev. January 2024), Dividends and Distributions, is filed by payers to report dividends and distributions paid to recipients and submitted to the Internal Revenue Service Center along with Form 1096.

Form 1099-G (Certain Government Payments) is issued by government agencies to report certain payments made to recipients, including unemployment compensation, state/local tax refunds, taxable grants, agriculture payments, and other government transfers, filed with the IRS.
Form 1099-INT (Rev. January 2024) is an IRS information return filed by payers (such as banks and financial institutions) to report interest income paid to a recipient during the calendar year.

Form 1099-K (Payment Card and Third Party Network Transactions, Rev. December 2026) is filed by payment settlement entities or electronic payment facilitators to report gross payment card and third-party network transaction amounts paid to a payee to the Internal Revenue Service.
Form 1099-MISC (Miscellaneous Information) is filed by payers to report miscellaneous payments such as rents, royalties, other income, and nonemployee compensation to recipients and the IRS.

Form 1099-NEC (Nonemployee Compensation, Rev. April 2025) is filed by a payer (business or individual) to report nonemployee compensation and related tax information paid to a recipient during the calendar year.

Form 1099-R (Distributions From Pensions, Annuities, Retirement or Profit-Sharing Plans, IRAs, Insurance Contracts, etc.) is issued by a payer to report distributions made to a recipient from qualified retirement or insurance plans and submitted to the Internal Revenue Service.

Form 1099-S (Proceeds From Real Estate Transactions) is an IRS information return filed by the filer (e.g., closing agent, mortgage lender, or other responsible party) to report proceeds from real estate transactions to the Internal Revenue Service and the transferor.

Form 4868, Application for Automatic Extension of Time To File U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, is filed by U.S. individual taxpayers (including those out of the country) to request an automatic 6-month extension to file their federal income tax return for tax year 2025.

Form 941 for 2026 (Rev. March 2026), Employer's QUARTERLY Federal Tax Return, is filed by employers with the IRS each quarter to report wages paid, federal income tax withheld, and Social Security and Medicare taxes owed.
Form W-2 (Wage and Tax Statement) is issued by employers to report an employee's annual wages, tips, other compensation, and all taxes withheld to the IRS and the employee.

Form W-9 (Rev. March 2024), 'Request for Taxpayer Identification Number and Certification,' is filled out by a U.S. individual or entity to provide their correct taxpayer identification number (TIN) and certification to a requester who is required to file an information return with the IRS.

HIPAA Authorization for Use or Disclosure of Protected Health Information (PHI), as required under 45 CFR §164.508. Covers the six required core elements and two required statements mandated by the HIPAA Privacy Rule.

HUD Form 50058 (Family Report) used by Public Housing Agencies to report household composition, income, assets, rent calculations, and program eligibility to HUD for assisted housing programs including Public Housing and Housing Choice Voucher programs.

HUD Form 50059 (Owner's Certification of Compliance with HUD's Tenant Eligibility and Rent Procedures) — certifies household eligibility, income, assets, and rent calculations for HUD-assisted multifamily housing programs.

HUD-1 Settlement Statement — the standardized U.S. real estate closing disclosure used for residential mortgage transactions prior to the TRID rule (October 2015), itemizing all charges and credits to the borrower and seller.
IRS Form 1040-ES (2024) — Estimated Tax for Individuals, capturing taxpayer identity, payment voucher details, and estimated tax computation worksheet figures.

IRS Form 1040-SR, U.S. Tax Return for Seniors — the large-print variant of Form 1040 for taxpayers age 65 or older, covering filing status, income, deductions, credits, tax liability, payments, and refund or balance due for a single tax year.

IRS Form 1040-X, Amended U.S. Individual Income Tax Return, capturing original, net change, and corrected amounts across income, deductions, tax, credits, and payments, along with filing status, explanation of changes, and preparer information.
IRS Form 1065 Schedule B — Other Information. Schedule of the main IRS Form 1065 return, extracted as its own blueprint.
IRS Form 1065 Schedule K — Partners' Distributive Share Items. Schedule of the main IRS Form 1065 return, extracted as its own blueprint.
IRS Form 1065 Schedule L — Balance Sheets per Books. Schedule of the main IRS Form 1065 return, extracted as its own blueprint.
IRS Form 1065 Schedule M 1 — Reconciliation of Income (Loss) per Books With Income (Loss) per Return. Schedule of the main IRS Form 1065 return, extracted as its own blueprint.
IRS Form 1065 Schedule M 2 — Analysis of Partners' Capital Accounts. Schedule of the main IRS Form 1065 return, extracted as its own blueprint.
IRS Form 1095-A (Health Insurance Marketplace Statement) reporting coverage through the Health Insurance Marketplace, used to reconcile the Premium Tax Credit on Form 8962.

IRS Form 1095-B (Health Coverage) — reports minimum essential coverage provided to individuals by insurers, government programs, or small self-insured employers. Part I identifies the responsible individual; Part II covers employer-sponsored plan details; Part III identifies the coverage issuer or provider; Part IV lists all covered individuals and their months of coverage.
IRS Form 1095-C (2024) — Employer-Provided Health Insurance Offer and Coverage, reporting ACA health coverage offers and enrollment for a single employee.
IRS Form 1098-E (Student Loan Interest Statement) — reports student loan interest received by a lender from a borrower during the tax year. Required when interest received is $600 or more.

IRS Form 1098-MA (Mortgage Assistance Payments) reporting homeowner mortgage assistance payments made by a state housing finance agency (HFA) under the Hardest Hit Fund or Emergency Homeowners' Loan Program.
IRS Form 1099-A (Acquisition or Abandonment of Secured Property) — reports the lender's acquisition of or the borrower's abandonment of property securing a loan.
IRS Form 1099-B — Proceeds from Broker and Barter Exchange Transactions, one record per reported transaction or covered lot.
IRS Form 1099-C (Cancellation of Debt) — reports the amount of cancelled or forgiven debt that a creditor has discharged, which may be taxable income to the debtor.
IRS Form 1099-LTC (Long-Term Care and Accelerated Death Benefits) — reports payments made under a long-term care insurance contract or accelerated death benefits paid under a life insurance policy.
IRS Form 1099-OID (Original Issue Discount) — reports OID income, interest, bond premium, and related tax information paid to a recipient during the tax year.
IRS Form 1099-PATR (2024) — Taxable Distributions Received From Cooperatives, reporting patronage dividends and related payments made by a cooperative to a patron.
IRS Form 1099-Q (2024) — Payments from Qualified Education Programs (Under Sections 529 and 530).
IRS Form 1099-SA (2024) — Distributions From an HSA, Archer MSA, or Medicare Advantage MSA, reporting amounts distributed from a tax-advantaged health savings account to a participant.
IRS Form 1120 (U.S. Corporation Income Tax Return) — annual corporate income tax return reporting income, deductions, credits, tax liability, and balance sheet data for a domestic C corporation.
IRS Form 1120 Schedule J — Tax Computation and Payment. Schedule of the main IRS Form 1120 return, extracted as its own blueprint.
IRS Form 1120 Schedule K — Other Information. Schedule of the main IRS Form 1120 return, extracted as its own blueprint.
IRS Form 1120 Schedule L — Balance Sheets per Books. Schedule of the main IRS Form 1120 return, extracted as its own blueprint.
IRS Form 1120 Schedule M 1 — Reconciliation of Income (Loss) per Books With Income (Loss) per Return. Schedule of the main IRS Form 1120 return, extracted as its own blueprint.
IRS Form 1120-S (2025 revision) — U.S. Income Tax Return for an S Corporation.

IRS Form 1120-S Schedule B — Other Information. Lines covering accounting method, business activity code, S-election history, shareholder relationships, foreign ownership, and various yes/no information questions.

IRS Form 1120-S Schedule K — Shareholders' Pro Rata Share Items. Corporation-level totals of each pass-through item (income, deductions, credits, distributions) that will be allocated to shareholders via Schedule K-1 (separate blueprint).
IRS Form 1120-S Schedule L — Balance Sheets per Books. Beginning- and end-of-year balance sheet positions in two paired columns (b)/(c) and (d)/(e), respectively.
IRS Form 1120-S Schedule M-1 — Reconciliation of Income (Loss) per Books With Income (Loss) per Return. Brings book net income into agreement with taxable income shown on the return.

IRS Form 1120-S Schedule M-2 — Analysis of Accumulated Adjustments Account (AAA), Other Adjustments Account (OAA), Previously Taxed E&P (PTEP), and other equity accounts. Tracks year-over-year activity in each shareholder-equity account.
IRS Form 2553 — Election by a Small Business Corporation to be treated as an S corporation under IRC Section 1362.
IRS Form 2848 (Power of Attorney and Declaration of Representative) authorizing a representative to act on behalf of a taxpayer before the IRS.
IRS Form 4506-T (Request for Transcript of Tax Return) — captures taxpayer identity, transcript type, tax periods requested, and third-party designee information.
IRS Form 4562 — Part I: Section 179 Election (Lines 1–13). Extracts only the fields in Part I of the form (plus the shared taxpayer header that anchors any per-part extraction).

IRS Form 4562 — Part II: Special Depreciation Allowance and Other Depreciation (Lines 14–16). Extracts only the fields in Part II of the form (plus the shared taxpayer header that anchors any per-part extraction).
IRS Form 4562 — Part III: MACRS Depreciation (Lines 17–20). Extracts only the fields in Part III of the form (plus the shared taxpayer header that anchors any per-part extraction).
IRS Form 4562 — Part IV: Summary (Lines 21–23). Extracts only the fields in Part IV of the form (plus the shared taxpayer header that anchors any per-part extraction).
IRS Form 4562 — Part V: Listed Property (Lines 24–41). Extracts only the fields in Part V of the form (plus the shared taxpayer header that anchors any per-part extraction).
IRS Form 4562 — Part VI: Amortization (Lines 42–44). Extracts only the fields in Part VI of the form (plus the shared taxpayer header that anchors any per-part extraction).

IRS Form 5471 (Rev. December 2022) — Information Return of U.S. Persons With Respect to Certain Foreign Corporations, covering filer identity, foreign corporation identity, and all standard schedules (A through Q).
IRS Form 5471 Schedule C — Income Statement. Schedule of the main IRS Form 5471 return, extracted as its own blueprint.
IRS Form 5471 Schedule F — Balance Sheet. Schedule of the main IRS Form 5471 return, extracted as its own blueprint.
IRS Form 5471 Schedule G — Other Information. Schedule of the main IRS Form 5471 return, extracted as its own blueprint.
IRS Form 5471 Schedule H — Current Earnings and Profits. Schedule of the main IRS Form 5471 return, extracted as its own blueprint.
IRS Form 5471 Schedule I — Summary of Shareholder's Income From Foreign Corporation. Schedule of the main IRS Form 5471 return, extracted as its own blueprint.

IRS Form 5498 — IRA Contribution Information, reporting contributions, rollovers, conversions, recharacterizations, fair market value, and required minimum distribution information for individual retirement accounts.

IRS Form 5500-EZ — Annual Return of a One-Participant (Owners/Partners and Their Spouses) Retirement Plan or a Foreign Plan. Used by owner-only or owner-and-spouse plans not required to file Form 5500.
IRS Form 56 (rev. December 2019) — Notice Concerning Fiduciary Relationship, used to notify the IRS of the creation or termination of a fiduciary relationship.
IRS Form 720 (Quarterly Federal Excise Tax Return) — reports federal excise taxes owed across Part I, Part II, and summary (Part III) for a single calendar quarter.

IRS Form 8606 (Nondeductible IRAs) — reports nondeductible traditional IRA contributions, basis tracking, and taxable amounts from IRA distributions, Roth conversions, and distributions from Roth IRAs.
IRS Form 8821 (Tax Information Authorization) authorizing a designee to inspect or receive confidential tax information on behalf of the taxpayer.
IRS Form 8825 (Rev. December 2025) — Rental Real Estate Income and Expenses of a Partnership or an S Corporation, reporting up to eight rental properties (columns A through H).
IRS Form 8829 (Expenses for Business Use of Your Home) — single-record extraction covering Parts I through IV of the home office deduction computation.
IRS Form 8832 (Entity Classification Election) — used by eligible entities to elect or change their federal tax classification for federal tax purposes.

IRS Form 8867 (Paid Preparer's Due Diligence Checklist) — used by paid tax preparers to document compliance with due diligence requirements for the Earned Income Credit (EIC/EITC), Child Tax Credit/Additional Child Tax Credit/Credit for Other Dependents (CTC/ACTC/ODC), American Opportunity Tax Credit (AOTC), and Head of Household (HOH) filing status.
IRS Form 8889 — Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) — reports HSA contributions, deductions, distributions, and qualified medical expenses for a single taxpayer filing year.

IRS Form 8938 (Statement of Specified Foreign Financial Assets) — used by U.S. taxpayers to report interests in specified foreign financial assets when the aggregate value exceeds applicable FATCA reporting thresholds.
IRS Form 8949 (Sales and Other Dispositions of Capital Assets) — per-transaction rows reporting proceeds, cost basis, adjustments, and gain or loss for capital asset sales and dispositions.
IRS Form 940 (2023 revision) — Employer's Annual Federal Unemployment (FUTA) Tax Return.
IRS Form 944 (Employer's Annual Federal Tax Return) for small employers whose annual payroll tax liability is $1,000 or less, filed annually instead of quarterly.

IRS Form 990 (2025) — Return of Organization Exempt From Income Tax — the annual information return filed by tax-exempt organizations under IRC section 501(a), covering organization identity, financial summary, governance, and supplemental schedules.

IRS Form 990 Schedule A (Public Charity Status and Public Support) — used by organizations filing Form 990 or 990-EZ to report their reason for public charity status and to compute public support ratios under sections 170(b)(1)(A)(iv), 170(b)(1)(A)(vi), and 509(a)(2).

IRS Form 990 Schedule B (Schedule of Contributors) — lists contributors who gave $5,000 or more to an organization filing Form 990, 990-EZ, or 990-PF, including contribution amounts, types, noncash property details, and exclusively religious/charitable transfer information.

IRS Form 990 Schedule C (Rev. 2023) — Political Campaign and Lobbying Activities, reporting an organization's political campaign activity, lobbying expenditures, and section 501(c)(3) direct/indirect lobbying elections.

IRS Form 990 Schedule D (2023) — Supplemental Financial Statements, covering donor-advised funds, conservation easements, art and museum collections, escrow and custodial arrangements, endowment funds, land/buildings/equipment, investments in other securities, program-related investments, other assets, other liabilities, and reconciliation of revenue and expenses per audited financial statements with amounts per return.
IRS Form 990 Schedule J (2023) — Compensation Information for certain officers, directors, trustees, key employees, and highest compensated employees of tax-exempt organizations.

IRS Form 990 Schedule L (Transactions With Interested Persons) — reports excess benefit transactions, loans to and from interested persons, grants or assistance benefiting interested persons, and business transactions involving interested persons.

IRS Form 990 Schedule O (Supplemental Information to Form 990 or 990-EZ) — free-form supplemental narrative responses required or elected by the organization for specific parts and lines of Form 990 or 990-EZ.
IRS Form 990-EZ (2023 revision) — Short Form Return of Organization Exempt From Income Tax, filed by small tax-exempt organizations with gross receipts under $200,000 and total assets under $500,000.
IRS Form 990-N (e-Postcard) — annual electronic notice filed by small tax-exempt organizations with gross receipts normally $50,000 or less.
IRS Form SS-4, Application for Employer Identification Number, used by businesses and other entities to apply for a federal EIN from the IRS.

IRS Form W-2G (Certain Gambling Winnings) Rev. January 2026 — reports gambling winnings and any federal or state income tax withheld, issued by payers of gambling winnings to winners and filed with the IRS.
IRS Form W-2c (Corrected Wage and Tax Statement) used to correct errors on a previously filed Form W-2.
IRS Form W-4 (Employee's Withholding Certificate) — captures employee filing status, withholding adjustments, and employer information for federal income tax withholding purposes.

IRS Form W-4P (2024 revision) — Withholding Certificate for Periodic Pension or Annuity Payments, used by payees to instruct payers how much federal income tax to withhold from periodic pension, annuity, and similar payments.

IRS Form W-4S (Request for Federal Income Tax Withholding from Sick Pay) — used by employees to request a specific whole-dollar amount of federal income tax withheld from sick pay received from a third-party payer.
IRS Form W-7, Application for IRS Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN), capturing applicant identity, address, foreign status, and reason for application.
IRS Form W-8BEN — Certificate of Foreign Status of Beneficial Owner for United States Tax Withholding and Reporting (Individuals).
IRS Form W-8BEN-E — Certificate of Status of Beneficial Owner for United States Tax Withholding and Reporting (Entities).
IRS Form W-8IMY (Rev. October 2021) — Certificate of Foreign Intermediary, Foreign Flow-Through Entity, or Certain U.S. Branches for United States Tax Withholding and Reporting.
IRS Schedule 1 (Form 1040), Additional Income and Adjustments — 2024 revision, covering Part I (additional income, lines 1–10) and Part II (adjustments to income, lines 11–26).

IRS Schedule 2 (Form 1040) — Additional Taxes, 2023 revision. Reports alternative minimum tax, excess advance premium tax credit repayment, self-employment tax, household employment taxes, and other additional taxes not captured on Form 1040 itself.

IRS Schedule 3 (Form 1040) — Additional Credits and Payments, used to report nonrefundable credits (Part I) and other payments and refundable credits (Part II) that are not entered directly on Form 1040.
IRS Schedule A (Form 1040) — Itemized Deductions, capturing all deduction categories and subtotals for a single tax year filing.
IRS Schedule B (Form 1040) — Interest and Ordinary Dividends, reporting taxable interest income, ordinary dividends, and foreign account / trust disclosures.

IRS Schedule C (Form 1040) — Profit or Loss From Business (Sole Proprietorship), used by sole proprietors to report business income, expenses, cost of goods sold, vehicle information, and other expenses.
IRS Schedule D (Form 1040) — Capital Gains and Losses, reporting short-term and long-term capital asset transactions and computing net capital gain or loss for the tax year.
IRS Schedule E (Form 1040) — Supplemental Income and Loss from rental real estate, royalties, partnerships, S corporations, estates, trusts, and REMICs.
IRS Schedule F (Form 1040) — Profit or Loss From Farming, reporting farm income and expenses for a sole proprietor farmer or partner.
IRS Schedule H (Form 1040) — Household Employment Taxes, used by household employers to report Social Security, Medicare, FUTA, and federal income taxes withheld for household employees.
IRS Schedule R (Form 1040), Credit for the Elderly or the Disabled — 2023 revision, used to compute the nonrefundable credit for taxpayers age 65 or older or permanently and totally disabled.
IRS Schedule SE (Form 1040) — Self-Employment Tax, used to compute net earnings from self-employment and the resulting SE tax liability (Social Security and Medicare taxes).

IRS/DOL/PBGC Form 5500 (Annual Return/Report of Employee Benefit Plan) — plan-level annual filing capturing plan identification, characteristics, participant counts, financial data, and compliance information.

IRS/DOL/PBGC Form 5500-SF (Short Form Annual Return/Report of Small Employee Benefit Plan), used by small plans with fewer than 100 participants to report plan characteristics, financial condition, and compliance information for a single plan year.
IRS/FinCEN Form 8300 — Report of Cash Payments Over $10,000 Received in a Trade or Business.

LD-2 Lobbying Disclosure Report filed quarterly with the U.S. Senate Office of Public Records and the U.S. House Clerk under the Lobbying Disclosure Act of 1995, as amended, disclosing registrant and client identity, lobbying activity by issue area, covered officials, and income or expenses for a single reporting period.
Medicare Summary Notice (MSN) — the periodic statement sent to Medicare beneficiaries summarizing claims processed on their behalf by Original Medicare (Part A, Part B, or Part D).
OPM Form 71 — Request for Leave or Approved Absence, used by federal civilian employees to request and document leave or other approved absences.
SEC Form 10-K — annual report filed by U.S. public companies disclosing financial condition, results of operations, risk factors, and business overview for the fiscal year.

SEC Form 10-Q quarterly report filed by public companies with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, containing unaudited financial statements and management's discussion of results for a fiscal quarter.
SEC Form 11-K annual report for employee stock purchase, savings, and similar plans, as filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
SEC Form 13F — quarterly institutional investment manager holdings report, one row per reported security position in the information table.
SEC Form 144 — Notice of Proposed Sale of Securities Pursuant to Rule 144 under the Securities Act of 1933, filed by affiliates or holders of restricted securities intending to sell.

SEC Form 15 (Certification and Notice of Termination of Registration) — used by an issuer to terminate a class of securities registration under Section 12(g) or 12(b), or to suspend the duty to file reports under Section 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934.
SEC Form 20-F — annual report and registration statement filed by foreign private issuers with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

SEC Form 25 — Notification of Removal from Listing and/or Registration under Section 12(b) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. Filed by a national securities exchange or by an issuer to delist a security and/or deregister a class of securities under Section 12(b).

SEC Form 3 — Initial Statement of Beneficial Ownership of Securities filed by insiders (officers, directors, and 10% shareholders) upon first becoming subject to Section 16 reporting obligations under the Securities Exchange Act.

SEC Form 4 (Statement of Changes in Beneficial Ownership) — one record per reported transaction filed by a corporate insider (officer, director, or 10% owner) reporting changes in beneficial ownership of company securities.
SEC Form 5 — Annual Statement of Changes in Beneficial Ownership, filed by corporate insiders (officers, directors, 10% owners) to report transactions not previously reported on Form 4.

SEC Form 8-A (Registration of Certain Classes of Securities under Section 12(b) or 12(g) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934) — used by issuers to register a class of securities on a national securities exchange or under Section 12(g) of the Exchange Act.
SEC Form 8-K current report filed by a public company to disclose material events or corporate changes that shareholders should know about promptly.

SEC Form ADV — the uniform registration and disclosure form filed by investment advisers with the SEC and state securities authorities, covering adviser identity, business practices, ownership, compensation, and disciplinary disclosures.
SEC Form D — Notice of Exempt Offering of Securities filed by issuers claiming a Regulation D or Section 4(a)(5) exemption.
SEC Form DEF 14A (Definitive Proxy Statement) — executive compensation, board composition, voting matters, and shareholder meeting details.
SEC Form NT 10-K — Notification of Late Filing, used by registrants to notify the SEC that their annual report on Form 10-K cannot be filed within the prescribed time period.
SEC Form S-1 registration statement filed by companies seeking to register securities for an initial public offering.

SEC Form S-3 registration statement for securities offerings by eligible reporting companies under the Securities Act of 1933, covering cover page, fee table, offering details, and Part II information.
SEC Form S-4 registration statement for securities issued in business combination transactions, including mergers, acquisitions, exchange offers, and recapitalizations.
